lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Put Crestway before Lakeview in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The current order interrupts the reader’s understanding of the career timeline.

items.says: Use consistent wrapping and spacing in the final document.
items.because: The apparent manual line breaks split bullets mid-sentence.

items.says: Prioritize bullets for the job being targeted.
items.because: The résumé mixes supply-chain analysis, warehouse operations, delivery work, and routing.

items.says: Confirm the contact details are current and clickable unless they were anonymized for the review.
Add GPA, relevant coursework, or honors only if they strengthen the application for the target roles.
Clarify whether 30–40 deliveries describes a typical, peak, or average day.
items.because: That distinction may matter to the scale of the work.

items.says: Consider whether payment collection deserves space.
items.because: It is less relevant to many analyst roles than analytical or operational experience.

items.says: Use a tense consistent with work still performed in this current role.
items.because: The bullet uses a past-tense verb.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the wedding-preparation and cooler-stocking responsibilities.
items.because: They are different duties, and neither shows scope or impact.

items.says: Use a tense consistent with work still performed in this current role.
items.because: The bullet uses past-tense verbs.

items.says: Clarify what “owned” meant for the layouts and reports.
items.because: “Owned” is broad.

items.says: State what changed or what the work achieved, if substantiated.
items.because: The bullet gives no outcome.

items.says: Explain how and over what period the returns time was measured.
items.because: The before-and-after result needs context.

items.says: Specify your personal contribution to the returns-desk change.
items.because: The bullet says the findings led to the triage station.

items.says: Clarify whether the wait times are averages and give the measurement period and scope.
items.because: The basis for the 95-to-40-minute reduction is unclear.

items.says: Separate the inventory result from unrelated duties or cut lower-priority details.
items.because: The bullet is overloaded with supervision, safety, hiring, and certification work.

items.says: Clarify how much of the accuracy increase came from cycle counting.
items.because: Other changes may have contributed to the rise from 91% to 98.5%.

items.says: Define stockouts, the periods compared, and what the $1.9M inventory reduction represents.
items.because: The major metrics lack a clear measurement basis.

items.says: Give more detail about the seasonal forecast model and your contribution.
items.because: That phrase alone is insufficient for a technical or planning audience.

items.says: Distinguish this result from the food-bank forecast result or correct the overlap.
items.because: The scale and outcomes are nearly identical and risk looking like the same result claimed twice.

items.says: Give the comparison period and define what the 15% freight reduction measures.
items.because: It is unclear whether the figure concerns total spend, cost per shipment, or another measure.

items.says: Add a dollar impact if it can be verified.
Connect the reorder-point work to a measurable result or its relevance to target roles.
items.because: The bullet states no outcome.

items.says: Check whether this bullet is needed alongside the demand-planning bullet.
items.because: The two may overlap.

items.says: Clarify what changed as a result of the supplier scorecard, if there is evidence.
items.because: The bullet only says buyers used it.

items.says: Define “least reliable” using the metric tracked.
An OEE figure of 112% is invalid under the standard definition.
items.because: Standard OEE is generally capped at 100%, so the figure raises questions about its definition or calculation.

items.says: Explain why doubling work-in-process was an acceptable tradeoff, or reconsider the result.
items.because: It could imply excess inventory, congestion, hidden costs, or a tradeoff rather than an improvement.

items.says: Explain what planned route miles included and whether current routes were measured on the same basis.
items.because: The 18% comparison needs to be fair and clear.

items.says: Describe what you built and how you modeled the routing problem.
items.because: Listing Python in the project title does not establish the technical work or your individual contribution.

items.says: Explain how the 5% drive-time comparison was calculated and whether routes and conditions were comparable.
items.because: The validation basis is unclear.

items.says: Give the pilot’s outcome, if available.
items.because: The bullet describes a two-truck pilot but no result from it.

items.says: Distinguish the model’s projected improvement from what the pilot established.
items.because: The pilot is not shown to have achieved the projected result.

items.says: Specify what the analysis and recommendations involved, or omit the bullet if the others cover them.
items.because: The description is too broad to show what you did.

items.says: Explain how the one-day gain was measured and whether it applied consistently.
items.because: It may have occurred only in particular cases.

items.says: Distinguish this forecast result from Crestway’s or correct the overlap.
items.because: The scale and outcomes are nearly identical and risk looking like the same result claimed twice.

items.says: Clarify how stockouts and inventory were measured.
items.because: The result lacks a clear measurement basis.

items.says: Indicate what you can do with Excel and Python, where supportable.
items.because: The tools list gives no indication of your capabilities.

items.says: Back each broad method with a specific example elsewhere, especially vehicle routing.
items.because: The routing project does not make that experience clear enough to support the listed skill.
